title: Training Leaves Traces: Reading a Model's Ancestry From Its Weights
hook: Open weights get fine-tuned, quantized, pruned and merged with no paper trail. This work finds a data-free signature in the weights that says whether two checkpoints share an ancestor.
key_points: Task: data-free white-box lineage verification — decide shared ancestry from weights alone, no inference required.
Residual training creates a shared identity-aligned component in branch products, so that structure alone proves nothing.
Removing it and comparing the checkpoint-specific structure across residual blocks yields a symmetric lineage score.
The score is calibrated against independent checkpoints, separating descendants from unrelated models at AUROC 1.0 on their benchmarks.
It distinguishes weight ancestry from mere behavioral similarity — distilled models read as unrelated.
Survives function-preserving 'checkpoint laundering' that breaks weight-space baselines, and runs 76x faster than the nearest robust one.
content_html: An open-weight model in the wild has usually been through several hands: fine-tuned, LoRA-merged, pruned, quantized, merged again. The provenance is rarely documented. Thakur and Khoury ask whether the weights alone give it away — no training data, no probing inputs, just two compatible checkpoints and a question about shared ancestry.
extra_html:
How it works

The obvious signal is a trap. Residual training produces a shared identity-aligned component in branch products, present in any compatible pair, so it can't establish ancestry. The method removes that component and compares what remains — the checkpoint-specific structure across residual blocks — into a symmetric lineage score, calibrated against independent checkpoints so the threshold is meaningful.

Why it matters

On residual-MLP and GPT-2 benchmarks the score cleanly separates fine-tuned, LoRA-merged, pruned and quantized descendants from independent and distilled models at AUROC 1.0 — meaning it reads weight ancestry rather than behavioral resemblance, which is exactly the distinction a provenance claim needs. Under function-preserving "checkpoint laundering," weight-space baselines lose their margin or fail outright while this score stays put, and it runs 76x faster than the nearest robust baseline on GPT-2. The authors report the projection-pairing signal appears across six model families, and a case study correctly sorts 3 related from 7 unrelated public LLaMA-2 checkpoints.

related.title: WARP: Weight-Space Analysis for Recovering Training Data Portfolios
related.hook: Labs rarely disclose their data mixture recipes — but WARP shows you can recover a fine-tuned model's training-domain proportions just from its released weights, no training data required.

related.title: Distilling the Knowledge in a Neural Network
related.hook: A big model's softened probabilities say more than hard labels - they reveal how classes relate, so training a small model to mimic them transfers knowledge a one-hot target never could.

flashcards.prompt: Why can't you establish ancestry just by finding shared structure in two checkpoints' residual branch products?
flashcards.back_html: Residual training itself produces a shared identity-aligned component in those products. Every compatible model has it, so its presence carries no information about lineage.

flashcards.prompt: Why do distilled models score as *unrelated* under this lineage signal?

choices.text: The score tracks weight ancestry, not behavioral similarity — distillation copies behavior, not weights
Distilled models are always smaller, so the checkpoints aren't compatible

flashcards.explanation_html: Separating provenance from behavior is the point: fine-tuned, LoRA-merged, pruned and quantized descendants are detected, while a model that merely imitates is not.

flashcards.prompt: What is 'checkpoint laundering' in this paper, and how does the proposed score hold up?

choices.text: Function-preserving transformations meant to hide provenance; the score is unchanged while weight-space baselines lose margin or fail
Retraining on synthetic data until the weights drift; the score degrades gracefully
Publishing weights under a new license; the score is irrelevant

flashcards.explanation_html: Laundering applies transformations that preserve the model's function. The authors report their score is unaffected and runs 76x faster than the nearest robust baseline on GPT-2.
